title: Anyone else using ripped assets for private game dev projects? What's your long-term plan?
author: HybridPepe
selftext:
I've found that even paid asset packs rarely give you a complete, cohesive foundation. Models, animations, sounds, and the overall visual vibe are pretty hard to get right. There's almost always a lot of manual work or custom commissioning needed to make everything fit together.

I had an old MMO from the 2000s in mind for a personal project, so I decided to see if I could rip its assets. Turns out it's easy to extract pretty much everything: models, animations, keyframes, effects, sounds, icons, maps, all wired together. Exported them all into a Godot project, built a viewer tool.

I ended up building my own game around them in a different genre. The original was an MMO, mine is a single-player ARPG, built with the same assets, but custom UI, systems, gameplay.

Obviously, this is strictly a private project. No plans to sell or distribute it, except from sharing with a few close friends (who are not even into this genre lol).

My hope is that AI will eventually make modeling and animation good enough that I can replace everything with non-licensed assets. Sound is probably the biggest pain point right now, though. Finding good sound effects that fit the game is the most time consuming part.

Anyone else doing something similar? What are you building, and are you planning to replace assets like this, or are you satisfied with just developing for yourself?
